students.name: Aiden

communication_style.description: Responds best to picture cards and a visual schedule. Verbal-only instructions are often missed.

sensory_triggers.reaction: Clamps hands over ears, may cry or rock

sensory_triggers.trigger: Unexpected touch when adjusting bow hold
sensory_triggers.reaction: Flinches and pulls the arm away

preferred_reinforcers: Listening to 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star' for 1 minute
calming_strategies: Move to the quiet corner of the room
Count to 10 together, slowly, holding up fingers

students.name: Mira

communication_style.description: Uses an AAC tablet to request breaks or express 'stop'/'more'. Minimal spoken language.

sensory_triggers.reaction: Freezes, then tries to bolt from the chair

sensory_triggers.trigger: Being asked to hold the instrument for more than 3 minutes without a break
sensory_triggers.reaction: Drops the violin or pushes it away

preferred_reinforcers: Praise via AAC device 'good job' button playback
Choosing the next activity picture card
calming_strategies: Offer the AAC device immediately and wait for a response
Deep pressure hug (only if pre-approved by parent)
Switch to pizzicato (plucking) instead of bowing to lower volume

students.name: Noah

communication_style.description: Strong verbal skills but needs short, literal instructions — avoid idioms like 'give it some space'.

sensory_triggers.trigger: Being corrected mid-piece / interrupted while playing
sensory_triggers.reaction: Refuses to continue, may argue or shut down

sensory_triggers.trigger: Unstructured 'free time' with no clear task
sensory_triggers.reaction: Wanders off or asks repeatedly to leave

preferred_reinforcers: 2 minutes of choosing any song to play from a favorites list
Verbal praise naming the specific skill done well
Being 'teacher' for 1 minute to show a sibling/volunteer a note
calming_strategies: Give a 2-minute verbal warning before any transition
Let him finish the current phrase before giving feedback
Offer two structured choices instead of open-ended ones

students.name: Priya

communication_style.description: First/Then board works well. Prefers written or drawn instructions over spoken ones.

sensory_triggers.trigger: Rosin dust smell or sticky rosin on fingers
sensory_triggers.reaction: Refuses to touch the bow, wipes hands repeatedly
Becomes distracted, covers eyes, loses focus

preferred_reinforcers: Drawing a note on the whiteboard after each success
Extra sticker for the First/Then board
calming_strategies: Offer a wet wipe for hands before continuing
Dim or reposition lighting if possible, or move seats
Reset with the First/Then board to show what comes next
